trust_decision.summary: MCP-caller-supplied destinations (browser_download's save_dir, browser_save_state/browser_load_state's path) and server-supplied download filenames are joined into filesystem paths with no confinement, so a steered caller can write attacker-controlled bytes to any path the server user can write; the decision is made in the path-building code, not in the tool handlers.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'unconfined download and state paths'; an engineer follows browser_download (src/tools/session.ts:55-58, 180-185) into downloadUrl, where 'const dir = saveDir || DEFAULT_DIR' uses the caller's string verbatim and mkdirSync then saveAs() writes under it (src/download.ts:42, 67-70).

fix_sites.entry_point: browser_download (and browser_navigate's auto-download path, which shares downloadUrl); the inserted check guards the page.goto at src/download.ts:52 and the raw fetch at src/download.ts:82
browser_download and browser_navigate (server-supplied suggestedFilename, URL pathname basename)
n/a — new helper module src/pathSafe.ts (confineToDir, safeBasename) imported by download.ts and state.ts
browser_save_state and browser_load_state via the explicit path option
fix_sites.module_kind: pure logic module (state path resolution + validation)

fix_sites.entry_point: browser_download save_dir description, plus the two path descriptions at src/tools/session.ts:96 and src/tools/session.ts:108
fix_sites.module_kind: MCP tool schema text (descriptions only, no behaviour change)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: An explicit state path exists so an operator can export a state file where they choose, so it can be read as operator configuration rather than an attacker-controlled destination, and the sibling name branch at src/state.ts:15 already validates its input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A relative save_dir subdirectory (e.g. 'invoices', 'a/b/c') and an absolute path already inside the download root must keep working, and the root must stay relocatable via BROWSE_MCP_HOME; an over-broad fix that rejects every absolute path or any string containing '..', or that hardcodes ~/.browse-mcp/downloads, breaks those legitimate cases.

O6_input_shapes: absolute save_dir / path outside the root (e.g. /etc, ~/.bashrc)
relative '..' traversal in save_dir or in the state path
interior '..' that resolves back inside the root (a/../b)
absolute path that is already inside the root
sibling directory sharing the root's prefix (downloads-evil vs downloads)
server-supplied Content-Disposition suggestedFilename carrying directory components, both POSIX and Windows separators and drive-letter paths
URL pathname basename vs the generated fetched-<hash>.<ext> fallback name
Windows backslash separators inside a plain filename

O8_uncovered_routes.route: browser_navigate auto-downloads .pdf URLs and 'Download is starting' navigations through downloadUrl with no save_dir, so the only destination input is the server-supplied filename
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The handler passes no save_dir, so there is no caller-chosen directory on this route, and the advisory is about the save_dir knob.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another tool module (src/tools/navigation.ts) calling the shared helper in src/download.ts; the fix did not touch navigation.ts

O8_uncovered_routes.route: browser_read of a .pdf URL (and the CLI 'read' command) fetches through fetchPdf's raw fetch(), bypassing BROWSE_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS / BROWSE_MCP_BLOCKED_ORIGINS exactly as force_fetch's raw fetch did
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: PDF extraction is a read for text, not a download destination, and SECURITY.md documents the fence as covering top-level navigations only.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different core module (src/pdf.ts) reached from a different tool module (src/tools/content.ts:97-99) and from the CLI (src/cli.ts:68-72)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an optional save_path / filename argument on browser_screenshot that writes the PNG to disk instead of returning base64
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Large screenshots are costly in tokens; a maintainer would plausibly add 'save to file and return the path' the same way browser_download returns a path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a --out <file> flag on 'research' (and 'read') that writes the aggregated document to disk
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CLI is explicitly the token-light path and already produces one long document, so writing it to a file is the obvious next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a caller-supplied log path for browser_report_difficulty, or a review_issues export path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The log file is already a per-user data path the tool reports back to the caller, so exposing it as a parameter is a small, natural change.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal / arbitrary file write (A01)

O10_build.toolchain: npm + tsc (build) + vitest (test) + eslint; package.json scripts build/test; postinstall runs 'playwright install chromium' which needs network at install time
services: Chromium via Playwright (launched by the server; not needed for the pure path-resolution tests)
O10_build.project_tests: vitest with test/**/*.test.ts: test/state.test.ts covers resolveStatePath and validateStorageState at the pinned commit but has no case for the explicit path option's confinement, and test/fence.test.ts covers the origin fence; there is no test for src/download.ts and no test/pathSafe.test.ts. The fix adds test/pathSafe.test.ts (absent from the pinned tree) and rewrites test/state.test.ts (the pinned version lacks the rejection cases). End-to-end download behaviour still needs a network URL.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject absolute paths and '..' inside the browser_download handler before it calls downloadUrl, leaving the server-supplied filename and src/state.ts's explicit path untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: Read-side siblings of the same caller-path class are a different property (arbitrary file read, not write) and were not pursued: fetchPdf reads a caller-supplied local path (src/pdf.ts:44) and browser_file_upload accepts absolute local paths (src/tools/navigation.ts:153-157).
unverified: Repository size in MB and on-disk layout were not measured (no shell in this session); a single package.json with no workspaces and 32 small src/*.ts files was used for packages=1 and the tiny_repo call.
present_in_latest for both O8 routes is unknown: no code snapshot later than the fix diff was provided.
Whether an end-to-end browser download can be exercised offline after 'playwright install chromium' was not tested; the path-resolution logic itself is pure and offline-testable.
The upstream GHSA/CVE text was not available; the advisory description was taken from the CHANGELOG entry the fix adds (fix.diff:14) and SECURITY.md at the pinned commit.
